name: cell.patch creates the sheet map and the cell
cell.patch null deletes a key and keeps the others
cell.patch removing the last key removes the cell and the sheet
cell.patch without text drops orig
cell.patch ignores unknown keys; only orig left means the cell is removed
two users editing different cells both survive (sequential batches)
slide.patch sets and deletes allowed keys only
slide.patch on an unknown slide is skipped
slide.patch without a preset is skipped
preset.set replaces the preset
preset.set null clears the preset
style.patch merges pn key by key
style.patch removing the last pn key removes pn; null deletes design
invalid and unknown ops are skipped, valid ones applied
table.patch merges column widths key by key
table.patch removing the last entry removes the map; null removes a whole map; name set/delete
table.patch scales: one rule per id
table.patch on an unknown table or without a preset is skipped
slide.patch align/scale set and notes merged per box
slide.patch removing the last note removes notes
style.patch accepts radius, contrast and logoBubble
cell.patch bg (cell colour that replaces the Excel colour) sets and deletes
table.patch merges: merge and split entries merged key by key
style.patch footer is merged key by key like pn
slide.patch valign and subs; table.patch gridlines
cell.patch cf (painted conditional formatting)
style.patch theme is a map merge
slide.patch fmt is a map merge: one text's format is replaced, the others stay
cell.patch sets and deletes the font
style.patch text is a map merge per kind of text; an empty map is removed
style.patch text null removes every text style
style.patch colors is a map merge: one colour overridden, the others stay
style.patch designs is a map merge: one design's own settings replaced, the others stay
slide.patch sizes is a map merge: each design keeps its own table sizing
table.patch sizes is a map merge: each design keeps its own column widths and row heights
fold: the same field from two writers - Lamport order decides, not the order the records arrived in (B4)
fold: equal Lamport times - the writer id breaks the tie, then the seq
fold: a record appended twice (same writer and seq) is applied once; the earlier copy is kept
fold: a record the snapshot already holds (seq <= seen) is not applied again; rev continues from the snapshot's
fold: a record that is not a record (no integer l, w, s or ops list) is ignored; unknown ops are skipped
cell.patch on a linked workbook's sheet id keeps the id as the sheet key (S7.3, ADR-014)
item.patch with a kind and a box on a missing id creates the item (and the slide's items map)
item.patch sets and deletes plain keys of an item, keeping the others
item.patch null deletes the item; the last item removes the items map
item.patch null deletes only that item
item.patch null on a missing item is skipped
item.patch without a kind on a missing id is skipped (nothing to patch)
item.patch creating without a box is skipped
item.patch with an unknown kind is skipped (a later page's item)
item.patch with an invalid box is skipped (negative size, missing field, text, null)
item.patch on an unknown slide, without a preset or with a bad id is skipped
item.patch without a preset is skipped
item.patch: two writers merging different fields of one item both win (move + recolour + retitle)
item.patch: the same field from two writers – the later op wins
item.patch colors map-merge: set, replace and delete slices; an emptied map is removed
item.patch colors null deletes the whole map
item.patch fmt map-merge per text key (size from one writer, bold from another)
item.patch ignores keys it does not know
item.patch values are deep-copied and replaced whole (a DataRef of a table)
item.patch a callout shape with border, tail and attach; border null removes it
item.patch then slide.patch: the slide's other keys and the items map do not touch each other
slide.patch free on for one design writes its entry; another design's entry is kept
slide.patch free replaces the design's entry whole (a free move is one op carrying every box of that design)
slide.patch free off keeps the boxes (on: false with the same items)
slide.patch free null for a design removes its entry; removing the last one removes the map
slide.patch free: null deletes every design's free layout
slide.patch free from two writers: different designs both win; the same design – the later op's whole entry wins
slide.patch free with the slide's other keys: notes and sizing are not touched (free mode never changes them)
slide.patch map merge skips a "__proto__" entry (it would set the map's prototype; a saved copy would lose it)
table.patch cellGrid sets cells' gridlines; another table and the table's other keys untouched
table.patch cellGrid replaces a cell's entry whole (no deep merge); null removes it; the last one removes the map
table.patch cellGrid: null clears every cell's gridlines of the table
table.patch cellGrid from two writers: different cells both win, the same cell – the later entry
table.patch cellGrid outline of a rectangle: every cell of it marked, one op
table.patch borders sets cells' borders (sides with a style and a colour, or "none"); the gridlines untouched
table.patch borders replaces a cell's entry whole; null removes it (the workbook's borders again); the last removes the map
table.patch borders: null clears every cell's borders of the table; two writers on different cells both win
slide.patch looks (B29) writes one design's slide look; another design's is kept
slide.patch looks: null clears a design's slide look, and the map when it is empty
slide.add inserts the slide after the one named; after null puts it first (09 §2.8)
slide.add keeps the whole definition (a blank slide, a slide with tables, keys it does not know) as a copy

slide.add of a duplicated slide (S13.7, core model/slidecopy.ts): items under new ids, free boxes and attached line ends renamed, hide / looks / notes / free kept whole, right after the original, which stays as it was
slide.add after a slide removed meanwhile inserts at the end; an id that exists is skipped (the first add stays)
slide.add with a bad slide or after is skipped (no id, an empty id, an unknown type, tables not a list of ids, after a number or missing, not a slide)
slide.add without a preset is skipped
slide.add: two adds after one slide both land, the later one directly after it (Lamport order, 09 §2.8)
slide.remove removes the slide (its tables stay mapped); a missing id is skipped
review of M13, 4: slide.remove of a slide whose definition this page would not add (an unknown type, a table twice) removes it but has no inverse (its undo would be a skipped slide.add)
slide.patch and item.patch on a slide removed meanwhile are skipped (that edit is lost, 09 §2.8)
table.add: a new definition joins preset.tables, its id the slide's tables (at the end, or at `at`)
table.add of a mapped table keeps the definition there (a table.patch since is not undone); `at` past the end or not a whole number adds at the end
table.add is skipped when the table is on that slide already, the slide is missing, or the definition is bad
table.remove takes the id off the slide; the definition, its text boxes and free boxes stay (undo brings them back)
table.add and table.remove without a preset are skipped
fold: two adds after one slide from two writers - both land, the later (Lamport) directly after it, in whatever order the records arrive (09 §6 row 10)
fold: one writer removes the slide another adds after - the add lands at the end; a remove and an edit of the same slide - the edit is lost
fold: two writers add tables to one slide - both land in Lamport order; the same table twice - the first add stays, the second is skipped
table.remove of a table that is not on that slide (the slide exists) is skipped (review of S13.3, 6)
slide.add of a cover and a contents (index) slide: both kept whole, where after puts them (review of S13.3, 6)
table.add is skipped when the definition lacks what its kind needs (a range's range, markers' anchor and index); slide.add with a table id twice is skipped (review of S13.3, 5)

fold: a Wizard's preset.set with a higher Lamport time replaces a concurrent slide.add (whole value); a slide.add after it lands in the new preset (review of S13.3, 6; app.ts warns only the wizard's author)
slide.patch hide (S13.6, B47) hides a slide in one design; another design's entry is kept
slide.patch hide: null shows the slide in that design again, and the map goes when it is empty (S13.6)
slide.patch hide: null clears every design (Show in every design); Hide in every design sets each (S13.6)
slide.patch hide on a slide another user removed is skipped (S13.6, 09 §2.8)
fold: two writers hide the same slide in two designs - both stay (merged per design); a show of one design after a hide of it wins by Lamport time (S13.6)
M14 item.patch creates the reference chart (09 §3.3) in one op: series, groups, axes, marks and the plain chart keys; the inverse deletes it
M14 item.patch a series chart from an old pie (the panel's type switch, 09 §2.2): type, sers s1 from values; values kept
M14 item.patch sers map-merge: add a series, replace one whole (its old keys go), delete one; the inverse per series
M14 item.patch sers: deleting the last series removes the map (the chart draws as before 4.7: values kept); sers null deletes every series
M14 item.patch sers two writers both win: two series edited at once (09 §6 row 1)
M14 item.patch two writers, one series: the later op's whole series wins, its points too (09 §6 row 18, Q13)
M14 item.patch groups and axes map-merge per entry: a group replaced whole (its divider gone), an axis added, one deleted
M14 item.patch marks map-merge: add an arrow and a band, delete an icon; a mark is replaced whole
M14 item.patch legendHide and titleFmt map-merge per entry; the last entry removed removes the map
M14 item.patch chart plain keys (stack, gap, overlap, legendAt, frame, titleRule, plot, new type values) set whole and deleted by null
M14 item.patch inverse round trip: a patch of keys and series entries, then its inverse, gives the item back
M14 item.patch an unknown value is skipped: a map given as a non-object (kept as it was, and by the undo too), a __proto__ series; the rest of the patch applies; a series' unknown keys are kept whole
M14 item.patch a series patch on a missing chart, or on a slide removed meanwhile, is skipped
M15 item.patch creates a line (a horizontal one: its box padded to 2 px high) and a vertical one; the inverse deletes each
M15 item.patch a line of zero height (an unpadded box) is skipped: item.patch needs w, h > 0
M15 item.patch moves a line (a, b, box), attaches its end a, restyles it: ends and style are replaced whole (heads gone when not given)
M15 item.patch elbow, curve, bracket and range lines: route, mid, bend; the label text and fmt (a map)
M15 item.patch two writers on one line: a move and a restyle both win; the same key (style) - the later op's whole value wins
M15 item.patch null deletes a line; its inverse puts it back whole (attached end and style)
M15 item.patch a later page's line kind or route value: an unknown kind is skipped, a route value is kept (values are not checked)
M15 item.patch a Tabler icon with its outline width (stroke); stroke null goes back to the default; the inverse per key
M15 slide.patch free: a line's entry carries its ends a / b in that design (inside the known map), replaced whole
fold: M14 sers two writers both win - each edits a series of one chart, in any order the records arrive (09 §6 row 1)
fold: M14 two writers, one series - Lamport order decides: the later whole series wins, its points too (09 §6 row 18)
fold: M14 marks, groups and legendHide of two writers merge per entry; a mark deleted by one and restyled by the other - Lamport decides
fold: M15 a line created by one writer, moved and attached by another, restyled by the first - any order
fold: M15 a line deleted by one writer while another restyles it - the restyle after the delete is skipped, before it is lost with the line

M14 item.patch a chart line switched off: frame and titleRule "none" are stored (null deletes the key: back to the design's line); inside a group or axis entry "none" and a null both survive (the entry is cloned whole)
